claim: Lung cancer: average symptom-onset to treatment in Finland is ~155 days (patient >50 d, primary care 41 d, specialist care 58 d).
source: Yle MOT, reporting preliminary UEF study (Prof. Outi Kuittinen), 12 Oct 2026

claim: Comparable lung cancer symptom-to-treatment delay in Sweden: 107 days.
Comparable lung cancer symptom-to-treatment delay in Denmark: 67 days.
Finland lacks comprehensive national data on cancer treatment delays and has no national cancer quality registry, unlike other Nordic countries.
The next state budget allocates no money to improving cancer outcomes and cuts EUR 400,000 earmarked for the cancer quality registry.

THL guidance 21/2016: maximum 6 weeks from arrival of a suspected-cancer referral to first treatment; imaging, sampling and pathology statements each within 1 week; adjuvant therapy within 4 weeks of surgery.
THL 21/2016 measurement points: referral arrival, first doctor visit, placement in treatment queue, first cancer treatment.

National Cancer Strategy Goal 3 'Ensure equitable and effective cancer care' indicators include: patients get treatment within target times (THL 21/2016); regional and socioeconomic differences are available and used to steer services; reliable information on regional differences in diagnostic and treatment practices.

Strategy target: 5-year survival for poor-prognosis cancers reaches Nordic level (SE+NO average): lung +14 pp, pancreas +6 pp, liver +14 pp vs 2023 NORDCAN; cancer mortality -10% (13,300 deaths/yr today).
Lung cancer 5-year relative survival 2018-22 (men): Finland 16.7%, Sweden 26.8%, Norway 28.2%, Denmark 26.2%; Finland women 27.3%.
Finnish lung cancer quality-registry pilot 2019-2023: only 27% of patients went to curative treatment; regional differences in diagnostics.
Patient survey (n=684, 2024-25): ~1/3 felt diagnosis was delayed; 1/3 needed >=3 healthcare visits before diagnosis; 6% learned diagnosis from OmaKanta.
source: Suomen Syöpäpotilaat ry survey via Verkkouutiset

claim: From 1 Jan 2025 the non-urgent primary-care guarantee was relaxed from 14 days to 3 months (over-23s).
AVI (31 Oct 2025): non-urgent primary-care access in Länsi-Uusimaa wellbeing county was not lawful and equal in 2025; significant intra-county differences.

2024 screening participation: breast 81.6%, colorectal 73.5%, cervical 73.5%. Lowest counties: Helsinki, Vantaa-Kerava, Länsi-Uusimaa. Strategy target >=80% in every programme in every county. Recommended: evening/weekend slots, reasonable travel distance.
Breast screening 2020-21: 60% non-employed vs 87% employed; 63% non-domestic-language vs 82%; 66% lower education vs 85% higher. Lowest region Helsinki 73%.
5-year relative survival: lower education 64% (men) / 65% (women) vs higher education 77% / 78%; no significant regional difference.
568 physicians per 1,000 new cancer cases in Finland vs 679 EU average; 2,223 nurses vs 1,376 EU.
Denmark Cancer Patient Pathways (2008): median diagnostic interval 14 days shorter during and 17 days shorter after implementation.

Norway pakkeforløp (2015): codes at defined measurement points in patient admin systems; target 70% within max time, met nationally every year 2016-2025 for the diagnostic pathway; mandatory pathway coordinators.
Sweden SVF (2015): inclusion and lead-time targets (>=80% within lead times), national waiting-time database, annual national PREM survey, state performance payments (SEK 182.5M in Dec 2024).
England Faster Diagnosis Standard: diagnosis or rule-out within 28 days of urgent referral; only about half met on time per CRUK analysis.
Systematic review (59 studies): 70% of studies on time to treatment found a significant reduction with patient navigation; 71% improved adherence; 87% improved satisfaction.
Clinical cancer notifications at diagnosis cover only about 40% of cases.
Target: at least 70% of cancers diagnosed at stages I-II by 2035 (indicator for symptom-awareness communication and standardised referral criteria).

Roadmap 2.5.2: standardised referral criteria and symptom-driven pathways based on Danish/Swedish/Norwegian models, incl. direct investigation routes and rapid access; >=5 most common cancers + county pilots in 2026-2028, all major cancers 2029-2031 (owner FICAN).

Roadmap 3.1.2: cancer-specific pathways with target waiting times and coding practices for 5 cancers in 2026-2028, all major cancers in 2029-2031; indicator: patients treated within target times. Funded within 3.1.1 (EUR 5M/yr, EUR 25M over 5 years).
Roadmap 1.2.3: named cancer care coordinator model; EUR 100,000 for guidance in 2026-2028, adoption by wellbeing counties only in 2029-2031.
Roadmap 3.2.2-3.2.3: annual national peer review and benchmarking among wellbeing counties (EUR 300k) and mechanisms to act on deviations (EUR 3M).
Roadmap 1.2.2: patient experience targets NPS >80 and HoPP >4.7, collected and reported in all units, published openly 2029-2031.
Roadmap 2026-2031 total EUR 139.1M (Goal 3: EUR 49.73M). Strategy cost EUR 156M over 5 years, about EUR 5.5 per inhabitant per year vs Denmark EUR 13 and Sweden EUR 4; expected savings EUR 305M.
Cancer care cost about EUR 1.5bn in 2023, projected about EUR 2.6bn by 2035 (+74%) without action; ~38,000 new cancers/yr rising to ~45,000 by 2035.
Lung cancer quality-registry pilot (2019-2023): stage information was missing for almost half of patients.
Lung cancer: primary-care segment of the pathway is 41 days.
source: Yle MOT, reporting preliminary UEF study, 12 Oct 2026

claim: Lung cancer: patient segment is reported as '>50 days'; 56 days is the remainder of the 155-day total after primary (41) and specialist (58) care.

claim: Target days from one pathway step to the next (referral sent 2, received 2, first test 7, diagnosis 7, MDT 7, treatment 14). Tests, sampling and pathology within 1 week follow THL 21/2016; the other limits are a team assumption. They sum to 39 days, inside the 42-day target.
An open loop is flagged when a completed step has no booked next step after this many days (SOP-3, the process playbook).
NCCN Distress Thermometer: a score of 4 or more (0-10) indicates clinically significant distress and should trigger a call.
Flag a language or area when its median days from first contact to diagnosis exceed the county median by more than this many days.
Aggregate cells with fewer than 5 pathways are suppressed.
source: Common statistical disclosure practice; team setting

claim: A newly fast-tracked patient gets a first call from the coordinator within this many working days (SOP-2, the process playbook). New fast-tracks rank first until the first message is sent.
Norway pakkeforløp: target that at least 70% of patients are diagnosed within the maximum pathway time.
Sweden SVF: target that at least 80% of patients are seen within the lead times.
Roadmap 1.2.2 patient-experience target: NPS above 80.

In the 14-day forecast, a pathway with an open loop is assumed to wait a further 25 days (the lower end of the patient chase delay in the synthetic model) before its next step, unless the loop is closed.
A positive FIT with no colonoscopy booked within this many days is flagged (safety-net rule, the pathway notes). Shown as 'Day N / 14' on the coordinator's list.
A specialist unit accepts or returns a referral within this many days, visibly (Fast-diagnosis lane, the governance notes).
Reserved (ring-fenced) diagnostic slots per test type, county and working day in the prototype: two (08:30 and 13:00).
Triage target: contacts before referral at most 2 (process playbook §2).
SOP-6: an interpreter flag is set for every patient who does not speak Finnish, Swedish or English (target 100%).
SOP-2: a coordinator is named within 1 working day of T0 (target 100%).
SOP-3: no open loop older than 7 days (target 0).
Slips are resolved within 2 days (target: at least 90% of reported slips).
Share of report fields extracted automatically without a human check: 30% then 60% then 80% (roadmap 4.1.1 as listed in the process playbook). Target shown: 80%.
Actionable report findings closed (a next step booked): target above 90% (process playbook §4).
Stage recorded in at least 90% of diagnoses (roadmap 3.2.1 as listed in the process playbook).
Patients who know what happens next (PU4 yes): target above 90% (process playbook §1).
Finnish FIT programme, first local results: 79% of positive tests attended colonoscopy.
source: Relander et al. 2025 (first local results of the Finnish FIT programme)
